newsitem.title: GERMANY: HDW unaware of merger talks with Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: HDW unaware of merger talks with Thyssen.

text.p: A spokeswoman for German shipbuilder Howaldtswerke Deutsche Werft AG (HDW) said she was not aware of plans for a merger of HDW with the shipyards of Thyssen AG.
"If talks were being held I would know about it," the spokeswoman said in response to a Reuter enquiry.
News magazine Der Spiegel reported that HDW parent company Preussag AG and Thyssen AG planned to merge their shipbuilding subsidiaries in a company to be called Deutsche Werft AG.
Thyssen planned to integrate its subsidiaries Blohm und Voss AG and Nordseewerke in Deutsche Werft, the report said.
Spiegel also reported that Blohm und Voss was in talks with Portuguese competitor Lisnave-Estaleiros Navais de Lisboa with a view to cooperation or taking a stake.
HDW managers believe that a merged company would only survive if it were guaranteed orders from the German government, the magazine reported.
Spiegel released the report ahead of publication in Monday's edition.
